        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Disabled people are a significant part of every community, and councils’ decisions about the accessibility of their facilities and services can determine whether people are able to participate in community life.

In a new article, we look at how councils consider accessibility when planning new facilities or upgrading existing ones. Our work draws on a survey of councils, our review of three council projects, and discussions with disabled people and organisations that support the disability community.

We found that some councils are taking steps to improve accessibility, but their understanding of accessibility and disability needs varies. Many councils do not have clear information about how well their facilities are working for, or being used by, disabled people.

Engagement with the disability community that starts early, is accessible, and continues throughout planning and delivery helps councils to make more informed decisions and leads to better outcomes for everyone. Ongoing feedback from disabled people is critical to understand what works in practice, and to improve facilities over time.

The article shares practical insights that all councils can consider in their planning, engagement, and design work when they build new facilities or upgrade existing ones.
